And Why Are There So Maaaaaaaaaaany Games These Days?

Games are easier to create than ever before, and AAA games are harder to create than ever before. I think that might account for the "quality gap" that people tend to perceive nowadays. Honestly I've always felt that we have more good choices now than before when it comes to both indie games and AAA titles. I know I've seen co-op grow the past few years when it used to be harder to come by. It's all about sifting through what you're not interested in to find what you really want to play.

That's what keeps me interested in gaming, tbh. You never know what you're going to find. I love it when I don't know that much about a game before I play it, and it turns out to be a little gem. Case in point was when I tried Dead Space 2. I knew the original had been popular, but all I really knew was that it was a horror game set in space. Turns out that I found it one of the most immersive gaming experiences of my life. I was literally sat with my face two inches from the screen, getting right into it.

And I think that's a great perspective to have. After all, who could have predicted Minecraft? The next big thing might not necessarily be something we'd expect, and that keeps me interested in some of these emerging areas like Vitrual Reality.
